text:
Riley M.: Pushed a new variant for the latency panel: p95 line on top of heatmap + compact time picker to the left. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc-latency-panel
Nora S.: Seeing it now. My first read: stacked p95 over heatmap feels noisy when traffic is high. Maybe show a subtle outline instead of full stroke at high density?
Ethan V.: Agree. Also the p95 label overlaps the scrubber handle at certain widths. Can we move the label to the top-left with a dashed connector line?
Priya: Copy point: current tooltip says "p95 latency". Suggest "p95 latency (95th percentile)" for clarity in help center tooltips.
Leo G.: Accessibility: the dashed connector must meet contrast ratio; dashed lines sometimes fail in WCAG tests. Consider a faint filled caret background behind the label instead.
Riley M.: Good call. Two layout options: A) overlay p95 with outline + small label top-left B) separate p95 in a thin header row above heatmap. Thoughts?
Nora S.: Option B gives breathing room and avoids collision with scrubber, but uses vertical real estate. If we do B, collapse at narrow widths to A with smart collision detection.
Ethan V.: For the time picker, inline presets are nice but keyboard users expect predictable order. Proposed order: presets -> custom range -> aggregation. Tab order should follow visible left-to-right.
Priya: On aggregation naming: earlier threads used "Aggregation"; here I propose "Bucket size" because it's more concrete for users who think in time windows.
Leo G.: "Bucket size" works. Tooltip: "Size of each heatmap bucket (larger = coarser)". Also add aria-describedby linking to the help text element.
Riley M.: UX interaction: when users drag the scrubber fast, we should throttle visual updates to the p95 overlay to avoid jank — 60fps target, but skip recalculation if scrubber velocity high.
Nora S.: Microcopy: the small settings gear currently says "Options". Change to "Display" to make it clearer it's visual controls, not data filters.
Ethan V.: Visual accessibility: heatmap color scale needs an off-switch for users who prefer lines-only. Add a toggle "Show heatmap" in Display panel.
Priya: QA checklist item: keyboard-only users must be able to open the Display panel, toggle heatmap, and change bucket size without a mouse. Add step-by-step tests.
ux-bot: Reminder: add storybook examples for p95 overlay + heatmap toggled off/on. Tag: @riley-m for component variant.
Leo G.: Contrast for the label: use #0b1a2b on 80% white bubble to pass 4.5:1 for small text. I'll add color tokens in the figma.
Riley M.: Decision: go with option B (header row) for desktop, fallback to A for mobile; rename to "Bucket size"; change gear label to "Display"; add heatmap toggle; ensure keyboard flow. I'll update the spec and post the dev handoff.
Nora S.: I'll write the accessibility notes and add the keyboard QA steps.
Ethan V.: I'll prototype the throttling logic and add a ticket for perf testing.
Priya: I'll update help center copy and add the tooltip wording.
Riley M.: Thanks team 44d I'll upload the final figma frame and include the ARIA example for bucket size control.
